prize_parts.citation: For a visionary Romanian-language prose oeuvre, rooted in a poet's attention to the sentence, that builds memory, the body and dream into a cumulative metaphysical architecture of rare imaginative scale.

statement.case_for: My laureate is unchanged: Mircea Cărtărescu (B006). My citation has changed. In round 1 I wrote a citation for a prose and poetic oeuvre. After the exchange I would centre it on the prose project, with the poetry named only as its origin. I make that change because of the evidence, not because colleagues ranked him first. The distinctive voice, the formal ambition of Blinding (the first volume of the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid, and the way memory, the body, dream and cosmology are built into one imaginative system are the part of the case I can state most concretely from public knowledge. They support a claim of sustained imaginative and intellectual depth under the common criteria. The poetry is the part of the oeuvre I can say least about, and a citation should claim only what the committee can defend. The chair asked whether the claim rests on the whole oeuvre or on the central novels. I think the honest answer is that the architecture of the large prose works carries it, and that the lyric origins explain the sentence-level texture. I have not read the texts and cannot verify them independently. My assessment rests on public knowledge and on colleagues' descriptions.
statement.case_against: The reservation I cannot remove is that the claim concerns Romanian sentence rhythm, density and patterned imagery, which I can judge only through translation and secondary description. Length is not evidence of quality. Whether the later long works enlarge the project or restate its motifs remains an open question. I cannot name particular passages or volumes that settle it, and I will not pretend that I can. If expert reports on the Romanian prose showed that the texture does not hold across the corpus, or that the later books mainly restate the earlier ones, my preference would move to Adonis (B005). On formal and linguistic renewal of a whole poetic language, his is the strongest competing claim. For now that would be a conditional shift. Nothing in the supplied evidence is strong enough for me to prefer no award (P000) over a laureate.

responses.point: Palm would keep the Cărtărescu citation to the novelistic project, so that the claim does not rest on poetry whose coverage in translation is thinnest. She also wants the citation to name the formal architecture and not only the imagery. She argues that the translation risk applies to every stylist on the list and should not lower his ranking.
responses.response: I accept the citation point and have changed my wording to match it. The prose project is where I can state the evidence, and the poetry belongs in the citation only as the source of the sentence-level texture. I agree that translation risk should not by itself reorder the candidates, because it affects Adonis and Zurita at least as much. I add one caution. A risk shared by every candidate does not make each case equally verifiable. It is a reason for the committee to say openly that it is judging the prose through translation, and not a reason to treat the uncertainty as settled. I also take her point that the citation should name the cumulative architecture, so I have put 'cumulative metaphysical architecture' in the wording.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg says the major novels should not be treated as a proxy for the whole oeuvre, and that a long, ambitious book should not count as sustained quality by size alone. He also says that expert reports on the Romanian prose would let him move from a provisional to a firmer view, and that expert testimony on Adonis's prosody would move him closer to Adonis.
responses.response: I agree with this, and it is the reason I narrowed my citation. Where I differ slightly is on the Adonis comparison. His being harder to verify in Arabic is a statement about the committee's evidence, not about the strength of the claim. The two should not be confused, and the chair's question about what would justify placing him first or equal turns on this. Reliable Arabic-language expert accounts of his prosody, his lexical choices and his dialogue with inherited forms would be the kind of evidence that could do it. Without that evidence I keep him as my first alternative. I accept Sem-Sandberg's other point: if the verse is the claim, then the essays and his public positions should appear in a citation only as related work, and a citation for Adonis should rest on the poems.

responses.point: Sward treats the length of the Orbitor trilogy and Solenoid as an open question. She says that size does not show sustained quality, and that her preference stays provisional until readers confirm that the later volumes develop the early ones. She also wants the citation to name the cumulative architecture.
responses.response: I share her provisionality. In answer to the chair's first question, I cannot name specific passages that would settle it, and I do not want to suggest evidence I do not have. What I can say is how I would test it. For each later volume, ask whether it widens the structure or the imaginative range of the project, or whether it returns to the same figures at a lower intensity. If expert readers found mostly restatement, my confidence would drop and the Adonis comparison would be reopened. For now I read the trilogy and Solenoid as an escalation of scale, but only as a judgment from public knowledge. That is a weaker basis than the one she asks for, and I have kept it marked as provisional.

responses.point: Olsson says that age is not a literary criterion for Adonis and that the committee's lack of Arabic competence limits confidence. He also says that Murnane's restricted range limits significance across a body of work.
responses.response: I agree on age, and I agree that it should play no part in the comparison for either Adonis or Cărtărescu. On Murnane I accept the point about range, and I record it as a change from my round-1 ranking: his formal severity is real, but a deliberately narrow range gives the whole-oeuvre claim less to rest on than Cărtărescu's cumulative architecture does. My fourth place for him on the opening ballot was a statement about the quality of his austerity, not about his significance across a body of work. I do not hold him as an alternative.

responses.point: Mattson calls Adonis a very close second on formal and linguistic achievement. She says her preference for Cărtărescu rests on how confidently each case can be assessed across the whole oeuvre from the evidence available, and not on any difference in seriousness. She also keeps Michon as an alternative because a slim corpus puts real weight on the breadth criterion.
responses.response: I think her framing is the right one, and I would adopt it as my own: the difference between B006 and B005 lies mainly in assessability, not in a verdict on seriousness. That makes my preference conditional on the evidence, which I have stated above. On Michon, in answer to the chair's question about concentration and breadth, I know of no stated standard that settles it. My working test is whether a compact body of work shows development and variety within its narrow range. The sentence-level achievement she describes is real, and I conceded in round 1 that compression is a legitimate form of achievement. Even so, the effect depends heavily on French syntax in translation. For a prize for the whole oeuvre I still place him below the candidates who give the committee more to assess, so he is not among my two alternatives.

uncertainties: I have not read the texts and cannot independently verify any claim. My judgments rest on public knowledge and on colleagues' descriptions.
How much of Cărtărescu's Romanian sentence rhythm and density survives in translation cannot be settled from the supplied evidence, and Romanian-language expert input is not available here.
Whether the later long works enlarge the project or restate its motifs is unresolved, and I cannot name specific passages or volumes that would resolve it.
The poetry and early fiction are unevenly translated, which is why I now centre the citation on the prose project.

Adonis's prosody and intertextual work, and Zurita's verbal texture, can be judged only through translation and secondary accounts. The difference between his case and Cărtărescu's may be a difference in evidence and not in merit.
My committee voting status as a co-opted member is undocumented, and my simulated vote is a modeling assumption.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted writer is apparent from the supplied profile. I disclose, without adjudicating, that I was elected to the Academy alongside Steve Sem-Sandberg in 2020, that I am married to a former finance minister, and that I have been Permanent Secretary since 1 June 2026. None of these facts is connected to any shortlisted writer on the supplied record, and I assert no recusal. My own non-fiction practice is context and not evidence of preference for any candidate. Whether a co-opted member votes in committee is not documented in the sources.
